why: Palindrome partitioning: the choice at each step is where the next piece ends. Choose a palindromic piece, explore the rest of the string, then un-choose it and try a longer piece.
hints: Every partition starts with some first piece text[0:end]. Which first pieces are allowed?
dfs(start): for each end in start+1..n, if text[start:end] is a palindrome, append it to the path, recurse on end, then pop. When start == n, record the path.
Collect all partitions and sort them (list comparison of strings gives the required order). With n <= 10 a direct palindrome check per piece is fine; for longer strings precompute isPal[i][j].
pitfalls: Comparison is case-sensitive: 'Aa' is not a palindrome.
Record a copy of the path, not the list you keep mutating.
